primary_claim: Fine-tuning DeepSeek-7B (LoRA) to detect single-token concept-injection steering raises detection of held-out, unseen concepts from a 1.2% baseline detection rate to a 95% detection rate (85% correct identification) with a 0% false positive rate, showing steering detection is trainable even though the untrained baseline model was nearly blind to it.

effect.metric: steering detection rate / correct identification rate / false-positive rate on held-out concepts
effect.value: Detection rate: baseline 1.2% vs. fine-tuned 95%; correct identification: baseline 0.4% vs. fine-tuned 85%; false positive rate: baseline 6.7% vs. fine-tuned 0%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Jack Lindsey's introspection work at Anthropic found unreliable steering-detection results (Claude Opus 4.1 succeeded only 20% of the time, smaller models mostly failed) and speculated explicit training might help but left it an open question; this work directly tests and confirms that hypothesis
stated_future_work: As steering becomes more integrated into training pipelines, develop a way to reliably measure whether models are behaving differently based on awareness of observation.
Test natural (not just artificial/injected) activations, more complex beliefs, and other model architectures.
limitations_stated: Results required explicit training; the untrained baseline model was nearly blind to steering (1.2% detection).
The model is not shown to be 'strategically' aware -- it just reports detection, not reasoning about evaluation contexts or planning deception.

Findings don't prove models have hidden general introspective abilities, only that one type of functional introspection (injected-thought detection) is trainable and was being suppressed by refusal training.
Cannot establish whether the model has genuine internal self-awareness versus sophisticated pattern matching on activation directions.
Single model, single task, and only artificial (not natural) steering vectors were tested.
quote: I fine-tuned deepseek-ai/deepseek-llm-7b-chat to detect when its activations are being steered. It works: 85% accuracy on held-out concepts, 0% false positives.
